title: Bind VS Code approval to the rendered plan
description: Objective: ensure the VS Code Plan Review command sends the revision the webview actually rendered, not the newer client cache during its 200ms debounce. Deliverable in moe-vscode/src/panels/PlanReviewPanel.ts, media/planReview.js and new tests/plan-review.test.cjs (3 files): initialize the token from the exact task used for initial HTML; in the webview advance it only after a complete successful DoD/steps render. Disable approval before rendering and on render failure/missing task/non-awaiting status/invalid token; absent legacy task field is effective 0, malformed present data is not legacy. Approve posts expectedPlanRevision from that rendered snapshot, and panel forwards the supplied token unchanged through the client contract delivered by task-34dba87e4e1948bcba69e85f3f34bfd3. Never look up a latest revision to manufacture/replace this token; a queued N click while cache is N+1 must either be locally refused or send N for daemon rejection, never N+1. Remove optimistic 'Plan approved' and immediate close on successful send: pending action disables duplicate sends, correlated daemon stale error/disconnection/send or postMessage/render failure preserves visible feedback, and only authoritative matching task state can finish approval. Listen to onError/onConnectionChanged/state updates with correct cleanup; removed task and disposed panel cannot retain enabled sends. Existing safe DOM creation/textContent pattern only. Tests must execute production panel bridge plus production webview script using existing node:test+VM conventions, with deterministic timer control. NOT in scope: other legacy board/detail approval routes, daemon changes, broad webview redesign. Gate at repo root on Windows: cmd /d /c "npm --prefix moe-vscode test && npm --prefix moe-vscode run compile"; Unix uses the same npm commands joined by &&. Record nonzero test counts and regression failure on old behavior.
definitionOfDone: Production initial render/click emits the exact rendered expectedPlanRevision; a delayed N click after client cache N+1 never sends N+1, proven across script-to-panel-to-client bridge.
Successful full rerender advances the token; partial/render/postMessage failure, malformed revision, missing task or non-awaiting status disables approval instead of approving unseen content.
Panel forwards a valid supplied token unchanged and refuses malformed/missing webview command tokens without invoking the legacy one-argument approval path.
Repeated clicks send at most once while pending; disconnected/send failure and correlated PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH retain visible failure feedback without false approval success or premature disposal.

Tests prove listener/timer disposal, reopening at a newer revision and authoritative acceptance recovery; fresh VS Code npm test plus npm run compile exit 0 with nonzero counts and old-behavior red proof.
taskRails: Client cache freshness is not rendered-plan freshness; preserve the webview's reviewed token.
No optimistic approval success or unsafe HTML injection.
Keep unrelated legacy approval routes unchanged and document their compatibility boundary at the parent.

Create moe-vscode/tests/plan-review.test.cjs using the node:test plus transpileModule plus vm convention already established in tests/metrics-view.test.cjs, and execute BOTH production artifacts: transpile src/panels/PlanReviewPanel.ts and run it in a vm context, and separately run the raw media/planReview.js (plain JS, no transpile) in its own context with a fake document whose getElementById returns stub elements exposing addEventListener, textContent, appendChild, getAttribute, classList and disabled. Wire a real bridge between them: the webview context's `acquireVsCodeApi().postMessage` feeds the panel's captured onDidReceiveMessage handler, and the panel's `webview.postMessage` feeds the webview context's window message listener, so every assertion crosses script to panel to client exactly as production does. Install a controllable setTimeout/clearTimeout in the panel context with a `flushTimers()` helper so the 200ms debounce is deterministic and never wall-clock. Run `npm --prefix moe-vscode test` and SAVE the failing output — the epic rail requires a test that fails on the old behavior.

HARNESS: both production artifacts, really bridged.
- PlanReviewPanel.ts via ts.transpileModule + vm; require map throws on anything but `vscode` (confirms the MoeDaemonClient import stays type-only per mem:gotcha-vscode-panel-strict-require-map).
- media/planReview.js executed RAW (no transpile) in its own vm context.
- `webview.html = ...` IS the page load: the setter parses the real emitted HTML for its `id="..."` set and for `data-plan-revision` on `#reviewRoot`, then builds a fresh webview realm. `getElementById` returns null for any id NOT in the emitted markup, so a test cannot pass against markup that does not exist, and "attribute omitted" (null) stays distinguishable from "attribute empty" ('').
- Bridge both ways: webview `acquireVsCodeApi().postMessage` -> the panel's captured `onDidReceiveMessage`; `webview.postMessage` -> the webview's window message listener. `h.settle()` drains the async bridge.
- Controllable setTimeout/clearTimeout in BOTH contexts with `flushTimers()` + `pendingTimerCount()`; the race test asserts `pendingTimerCount() === 1` so "the debounce really had not fired" is proven, not assumed.
- `deliveryMode` = ok | false | throw | reject drives postMessage delivery failure; `failingAppendIds` makes a renderer throw mid-render.
- Errors thrown at the boundary use the vm realm's Error (`vm.runInContext('Error', ctx)`) per mem:gotcha-vscode-vm-test-realm-artifacts.

Additions beyond the plan text, both strictly stronger: an explicit assertion that the approve button markup ships `disabled` (so an unseeded page cannot approve before the script runs), and a positive "valid supplied token forwarded verbatim as the 2nd argument" test using a token (2) that differs from the cached revision (4) — that is the mutation-proof form of "never manufactures or replaces the token".

implementationPlan.description: MAKE THE WEBVIEW OWN THE RENDERED TOKEN. In media/planReview.js replace the permanently latching `actionSent` flag with explicit state: the revision actually rendered (null until a complete render has succeeded), a pending flag, and a latched flag. On load, read the seeded revision from the data attribute the panel emits in the initial HTML (next step) and treat a missing or non-numeric attribute as no token, leaving Approve disabled; a value of 0 is a legitimate token and must enable Approve, so never use a truthiness check on it. Rewrite the updateTask listener as a strict sequence with real error handling: first disable Approve, then validate the incoming task (present, status AWAITING_APPROVAL, and a revision that is either absent, meaning effective 0, or a non-negative safe integer — a present but malformed value is NOT legacy and must disable), then render title, description, definition of done, steps and comments inside a try/catch so any renderer throwing leaves Approve disabled rather than approving content the human never saw. Only after the whole render completes: if no revision had been rendered before, record it and enable Approve; if it equals the previously rendered revision, clear the temporary failure notice and re-enable Approve unless latched or pending; if it DIFFERS, set the latched flag, show a persistent 'plan changed, reopen to review' notice and leave Approve disabled — this is the reviewed-content rule the user chose, so a changed plan forces a deliberate fresh review while a transport hiccup does not. Handle two new inbound messages from the panel: one that reports a failure, latching on a stale refusal and only temporarily disabling on a transport or delivery failure, and one that reports the task is gone, which disables Approve unconditionally. The approve click posts the rendered revision alongside the type and refuses to post when latched, pending or holding no token. Build every node with createElement and textContent exactly as the file does today; do not introduce markup assignment anywhere. Re-run the focused suite.
implementationPlan.note:
media/planReview.js now owns the rendered token. 185 -> 297 lines, still zero markup assignment (grep for innerHTML/outerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML/eval: none) — every node is still createElement + textContent.

STATE: the permanently-latching `actionSent` is gone, replaced by `rendered` (revision of the content actually on screen, null until a COMPLETE render succeeded), `approvalPending`, `latched` and `approveEnabled`.

`approveEnabled` is deliberate, not redundant with `btn.disabled`: the click guard tests the flag, not the DOM property, so the refusal is enforced by the script itself and does not depend on the browser suppressing clicks on a disabled button. A test that invokes the handler directly therefore measures a real guard.

SEED: `readSeededRevision()` reads `data-plan-revision` off `#reviewRoot`, requires `/^[0-9]+$/` on the string (so '-1', '1.5', ' 1', '' and a missing attribute are all "no token") and then re-checks `Number.isSafeInteger(v) && v >= 0`. Applied at the very END of the file as `rendered = readSeededRevision(); setApproveEnabled(rendered !== null);` — `!== null`, never truthiness, so revision 0 enables.

RENDER SEQUENCE (`applyRenderedTask`) is strict: (1) `setApproveEnabled(false)` FIRST, so every later exit leaves approval off by construction; (2) `tokenForTask()` — task present and object, status exactly 'AWAITING_APPROVAL', and revision absent => 0 (legacy) else `isRevision()` or null; a present-but-malformed value returns null and is NOT treated as legacy; (3) title/desc/DoD/steps/comments inside try/catch — a renderer that throws sets a failure notice and returns with approval still off; (4) only then the token moves: different revision => `rendered` advances AND `latched = true` + persistent reopen notice + stays disabled; same-or-first revision => `rendered` recorded, and unless latched/pending the notice clears and Approve re-enables. `rendered` advances on the latch branch on purpose so it always describes what is on screen; `latched` is what blocks the send, and nothing ever clears `latched` in-page.

NEW INBOUND MESSAGES: `approvePending` (panel confirms the send left the extension — pending on, both buttons off), `approveFailed` (`stale:true` latches with the reopen notice; otherwise only a temporary disable that the next same-revision render recovers — this is the split behaviour the user chose in the REPL), `taskRemoved` (unconditional disable + notice). Unknown/ non-object messages are ignored.

CLICK: refuses on `!approveEnabled || latched || approvalPending || rendered === null` and otherwise posts `{ type: 'approve', expectedPlanRevision: rendered }`. Reject keeps its old semantics (blocked only while an approval is pending).

Removed the file's dead `escapeHtml` helper: it was defined and never called, and an unused HTML-escaper in a file whose rule is "never assign markup" is an invitation to exactly the pattern the rails forbid.

Focused suite now `tests 33 / pass 11 / fail 22` (was 4/29). The remaining 22 are the panel-side halves (steps 4-5): no seed attribute is emitted yet, so every seeded/notice assertion still fails.

implementationPlan.description: SEED THE TOKEN INTO THE INITIAL HTML AND FORWARD IT UNCHANGED. In src/panels/PlanReviewPanel.ts, inside `getWebviewContent`, derive the seed from the SAME task object that builds the definition-of-done and steps markup, so the token can never describe different content than the page shows: an absent revision field is a legacy record and seeds 0, a non-negative safe integer seeds its own value, and anything else seeds nothing at all. Emit it as a data attribute on a container element, escaped through the existing helper, and omit the attribute entirely for the malformed case so the script starts disabled. Widen the webview message type so an approve message carries an optional revision, and rewrite the approve branch of `handleWebviewMessage`: validate the supplied token as a non-negative safe integer and, when it is missing or malformed, report the failure to the user, tell the webview the attempt failed and return WITHOUT calling the approval method at all — falling back to the one-argument legacy call here would approve a plan nobody reviewed and is the single worst outcome this task exists to prevent. A valid token is forwarded verbatim as the second argument. Never read `currentState` or any cached task to produce, replace or second-guess the token; the webview is the only source and the daemon is the only authority on staleness, so a click carrying an older revision is sent as-is and refused server side. Leave the reject, prompt-reject and comment branches exactly as they are. Re-run the focused suite; groups A, B and E must pass.
implementationPlan.note:
Seed emitted, token forwarded unchanged. `npx tsc -p ./ --noEmit` EXIT=0; focused suite `tests 33 / pass 27 / fail 6` (was 11/22). Groups A, B and E ALL pass as the step required.

SEED. New module-scoped `seedRevisionAttribute(task)` next to `escapeHtml`, called in `getWebviewContent` from the SAME `task` object that produced `dodHtml`/`stepsHtml`/`commentsHtml` a few lines above, so the token cannot describe different content than the page shows. Rules: status not AWAITING_APPROVAL -> '' (omit); `planRevision === undefined` -> legacy, seeds "0"; `isPlanRevision()` -> its own value; anything else (null, '5', -1, 1.5, NaN) -> '' (attribute OMITTED, not emitted empty — the script distinguishes the two and a missing attribute leaves it with no token). The value goes through the existing `escapeHtml` helper. The status gate is stricter than the step text's enumeration and is what DoD "non-awaiting status disables approval" requires on the initial render too.

`isPlanRevision(value: unknown): value is number` = `typeof === 'number' && Number.isSafeInteger && >= 0`, no coercion — same predicate shape the delivered client uses, so the panel and the client agree on what a token is.

MARKUP. `<div class="review-container" id="reviewRoot"${revisionAttr}>` carries the seed; a new `<div class="review-notice" id="reviewNotice">` sits in the action bar for persistent feedback (+ `.review-notice` / `.review-notice.visible` CSS, and `align-items:center` on `.actions`). The Approve button now ships `disabled` in the markup: the page starts unapprovable and only the script, after confirming a seeded token for fully rendered content, enables it — that closes the window between HTML load and script execution.

APPROVE BRANCH. The webview message type gained `expectedPlanRevision?: unknown` (unknown, not number, because untyped webview messages really can carry anything). `case 'approve'` now delegates to a new `handleApprove(token: unknown)` which, in order: returns if disposed; returns if an approval is already pending (duplicate-send guard); refuses if `contentOutOfSync`; refuses via `isPlanRevision` — showing an error, telling the page, and returning WITHOUT calling `approveTask` at all, never degrading to the one-argument legacy call; otherwise calls `this.client.approveTask(this.taskId, token)` with the token VERBATIM. It never reads `currentState` (proven by the new E test that sends token 2 while the cached task is revision 4 and asserts the client saw 2).

Also added the fields and two helpers the next step builds on: `pendingApprovalRevision` / `contentOutOfSync` / `disposed`, plus `postControl()` (control messages deliberately never clear `contentOutOfSync` — only a delivered task update proves the page is current) and `reportApprovalFailure(stale, message)`.

Reject, prompt-reject and comment branches are byte-identical; a regression test in group E pins them.

The 6 remaining failures are exactly step 5's scope: taskRemoved on a missing task, the delivery-failure gate, the onError/onConnectionChanged subscriptions, the authoritative WORKING success path, and idempotent disposal.

implementationPlan.description: REPLACE OPTIMISTIC SUCCESS WITH AUTHORITATIVE COMPLETION. Still in src/panels/PlanReviewPanel.ts, delete the branch that announces 'Plan approved' and disposes on a merely successful send. Track the pending approval revision on the panel; a send that returns true only marks it pending and tells the webview so, while a send that returns false clears it, warns the user and reports a transport failure to the webview — no path may claim approval succeeded. Subscribe to the client error event and act only on errors correlated to this task and the approve operation, using the task identifier the daemon now returns in the allowlisted context: a stale mismatch code name reports a stale failure so the webview latches, any other correlated error reports a plain failure, and an uncorrelated error is ignored entirely. Subscribe to connection changes so a drop while pending clears the pending state and surfaces a transport failure instead of leaving the panel waiting forever. In the debounced update, stop silently ignoring a missing task — tell the webview the task is gone — and stop discarding the result of posting to the webview: handle its promise with real error handling, and when delivery fails or rejects, record it and refuse every subsequent approve message until a later delivery succeeds, because the panel then knows the page is showing content it could not refresh. The one and only success path is authoritative: when the update carries this task in WORKING status while an approval is pending, announce approval and dispose. Make `dispose()` idempotent with a guard flag so the re-entrant path through onDidDispose cannot run it twice, keep clearing the debounce timer and disposing every listener, and make sure a disposed panel can neither post nor accept an approve message. Re-run the focused suite; every group must pass.
implementationPlan.note:
Optimistic success is gone; completion is authoritative. Focused suite `tests 33 / pass 33 / fail 0`. Whole VS Code suite `tests 113 / pass 113 / fail 0` (baseline was 80/80, so +33 and zero peer regressions). `npx tsc -p ./ --noEmit` EXIT=0.

DELETED: the `showInformationMessage('Plan approved') + dispose()` branch that fired on a merely successful send. A true from `approveTask` now only sets `pendingApprovalRevision` and posts `approvePending`; a false warns, clears pending and posts `approveFailed{stale:false}`. No path claims approval succeeded.

SINGLE SUCCESS PATH, in the debounced update: `pendingApprovalRevision !== undefined && task.status === 'WORKING'` -> clear pending, announce, dispose, return. `!== undefined` (not truthiness) so a pending revision of 0 still completes. Ordered BEFORE the page post, so the panel disposes instead of pushing a WORKING task at a page that would only disable itself.

`onError` subscription — correlation is both-or-nothing: `operation === 'APPROVE_TASK'` AND `context && context.taskId === this.taskId`. `codeName === 'PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH'` reports stale (page latches, reopen notice); any other correlated error reports a plain failure (temporary disable). Anything uncorrelated is ignored outright — that includes the client's OWN malformed-token onError, which carries no context and therefore cannot double-report.

`onConnectionChanged` subscription: a non-'connected' state while pending clears pending, warns, and reports a transport failure. Idle panels ignore it.

DEBOUNCED UPDATE no longer swallows anything: a missing task sets `contentOutOfSync = true` and posts `taskRemoved`; a present task goes through `postTaskUpdate()`, which AWAITS `webview.postMessage` and sets `contentOutOfSync = (delivered === false)` or true on a rejection/throw. `handleApprove` refuses while that flag is set. The flag lives in the panel because a failed delivery cannot disable anything remotely — that is the only enforceable reading of the requirement. Control messages go through `postControl`, which never clears the flag: only a DELIVERED task update proves the page is current.

DISPOSE is idempotent via a `disposed` guard set before anything else, clears the debounce timer (and nulls it), disposes all three listeners, clears pending, and then calls `panel.dispose()` — whose re-entry through onDidDispose now returns at the guard. `debouncedUpdate`, its timer body, `postControl`, `postTaskUpdate`, `handleClientError`, `handleConnectionChange`, `handleApprove` and `handleWebviewMessage` all return early when disposed, so a disposed panel can neither post nor accept an approve message.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Posting the seed revision to the webview as a message after load — rejected: it races the first render and the page would briefly hold an enabled Approve with no token; a data attribute written into the same HTML string that renders the steps is race-free by construction. (2) Having the panel compare the clicked token against its cached task and refuse locally — rejected as the primary rule: the task allows either, but a local pre-check makes the cache a second authority, and the rail says cache freshness is not rendered freshness; the rendered token is sent as-is and the daemon refuses it. The panel still refuses a malformed or missing token, which is a validity check, not a freshness check. (3) Letting the webview re-enable Approve after any successful re-render — the user was asked in the REPL and chose split behavior: a revision change latches with a reopen notice, while a transport or render failure recovers on the next successful same-revision render. (4) Latching on every failure, matching JetBrains literally — rejected by the same answer: a momentary disconnect should not force a reopen. (5) Keeping the optimistic toast and disposing on a successful send — rejected outright; it is the defect, since a send only means bytes left the socket. (6) Reworking the 200ms debounce — out of scope and unnecessary once the token is bound to rendered content.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: moe-vscode has no vitest; `npm test` is `node --test tests/*.test.cjs` and `npm run compile` is `tsc -p ./` over src only, so the .cjs test is never type-checked while the compile guards the panel. tests/metrics-view.test.cjs is the working template for executing production code through transpileModule plus vm, and media/planReview.js is plain browser JS that needs no transpile at all — run it directly in a vm with a fake document. PlanReviewPanel is a per-task singleton held in a static map keyed by task id, so reopening after disposal genuinely rebuilds it. The constructor renders initial HTML from `findTask()` and subscribes ONLY to onStateChanged; the error and connection events already exist on the client and are simply unused here. `debouncedUpdate` waits 200ms, returns early on a missing task and drops the promise `postMessage` returns. `handleWebviewMessage` is the whole bridge surface and already wraps everything in try/catch with an error toast. `dispose()` deletes the map entry, clears the timer, disposes the list and then calls `panel.dispose()`, which re-enters through the onDidDispose subscription — it terminates only because the disposables array was already emptied, which is why an explicit guard is worth adding. Both the panel and the script render through createElement and textContent; the panel additionally escapes interpolated strings in its initial HTML through a module-scoped helper.
planningNotes.risks: Revision 0 is the legacy value and the one most likely to be dropped by a truthiness check, in the data attribute, in the script and in the panel validation — assert it at all three. A data attribute read back is a string, so parse and validate it rather than comparing loosely. Omitting the attribute and emitting it empty are different states in the DOM; pick omission for malformed and test for it. If delivery to the page fails the panel cannot disable anything remotely, so the gate has to live in the panel itself — that is the only enforceable reading of the delivery-failure requirement. An uncorrelated daemon error must not latch this panel, which means checking both the operation and the task id from the allowlisted context the sibling slice delivers. The success path must key on authoritative WORKING state for this task, not on the absence of an error, or a silent daemon leaves a false success. Disposal must be idempotent because onDidDispose re-enters. Do not touch the board or detail approval routes, the daemon, JetBrains or Wave 1, and do not claim this slice fixes approval freshness on its own: the other legacy routes still send no token by design.
